knowledge_point.title: Determining an Intercept of a Tangent or Normal Line to a Curve Given in Implicit Form

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $x y + 2 y=-8$. The **tangent** line at $\left(0,-4\right)$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. The product rule gives $\frac{d}{dx}(xy)=y+x\frac{dy}{dx}$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y+\left(x + 2\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(x + 2\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(y\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{y}{x + 2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{-4}{2}=2
$$

The tangent line uses $m=2$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-4\right)&=2\left(x-\left(0\right)\right) \\
y&=2\left(x-\left(0\right)\right)+\left(-4\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=2\left(x-\left(0\right)\right)+\left(-4\right) \\
x-\left(0\right)&=-\frac{-4}{2} \\
x&=2
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(2,0\right)$.

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $2 x^{2} + 2 x - 2 y=6$. The **tangent** line at $\left(-3,3\right)$ meets the $y$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
4 x + 2+\left(-2\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(-2\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(4 x + 2\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{4 x + 2}{-2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{-10}{-2}=-5
$$

The tangent line uses $m=-5$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(3\right)&=-5\left(x-\left(-3\right)\right) \\
y&=-5\left(x-\left(-3\right)\right)+\left(3\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=-5\left(0-\left(-3\right)\right)+\left(3\right) \\
y&=-12
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(0,-12\right)$.

question.:question/worked-solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}
4 x+\left(2 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(2 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(4 x\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{4 x}{2 y}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{-8}{4}=2
$$

The tangent line uses $m=2$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=2\left(0-\left(-2\right)\right)+\left(2\right) \\

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $x^{2} + 4 x + y^{2} - 2 y=15$. The **tangent** line at $\left(0,-3\right)$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
2 x + 4+\left(2 y - 2\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(2 y - 2\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(2 x + 4\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{2 x + 4}{2 y - 2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{4}{-8}=\frac{1}{2}
$$

The tangent line uses $m=\frac{1}{2}$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-3\right)&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(0\right)\right) \\
y&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(0\right)\right)+\left(-3\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(0\right)\right)+\left(-3\right) \\
x-\left(0\right)&=-\frac{-3}{\frac{1}{2}} \\
x&=6
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(6,0\right)$.

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $x^{2} - 2 x + 4 y=-8$. The **tangent** line at $\left(4,-4\right)$ meets the $y$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
2 x - 2+\left(4\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(4\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(2 x - 2\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{2 x - 2}{4}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{6}{4}=- \frac{3}{2}
$$

The tangent line uses $m=- \frac{3}{2}$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-4\right)&=- \frac{3}{2}\left(x-\left(4\right)\right) \\
y&=- \frac{3}{2}\left(x-\left(4\right)\right)+\left(-4\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=- \frac{3}{2}\left(0-\left(4\right)\right)+\left(-4\right) \\
y&=2
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(0,2\right)$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
8 x+\left(8 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(8 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(8 x\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{8 x}{8 y}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{-24}{8}=3
$$

The tangent line uses $m=3$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(1\right)&=3\left(x-\left(-3\right)\right) \\
y&=3\left(x-\left(-3\right)\right)+\left(1\right)

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $x y + x=6$. The **tangent** line at $\left(-2,-4\right)$ meets the $y$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. The product rule gives $\frac{d}{dx}(xy)=y+x\frac{dy}{dx}$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y + 1+\left(x\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(x\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(y + 1\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{y + 1}{x}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{-3}{-2}=- \frac{3}{2}
$$

The tangent line uses $m=- \frac{3}{2}$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-4\right)&=- \frac{3}{2}\left(x-\left(-2\right)\right) \\
y&=- \frac{3}{2}\left(x-\left(-2\right)\right)+\left(-4\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=- \frac{3}{2}\left(0-\left(-2\right)\right)+\left(-4\right) \\
y&=-7
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(0,-7\right)$.
